subject: Burst allocator deadlock — reserved capacity queue starvation & action plan
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: GlyphTech SRE <sre@glyphtech.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected sustained latency & 502s from reserved GPU pool (GlyphTech-prod)

Hi Priyom —

Starting around 2:45pm PT we've been seeing sustained 95th/99th latency spikes and intermittent 502s for our production inference endpoints backed by the reserved GPU pool (pool-id: rsv-glyph-prod-03). Traffic hasn't changed on our side. The errors have continued for ~25 minutes and are impacting critical workflows (real-time ranking).

Our SRE team collected traces and saw queuing build-up on the serving tier. Can Redwood confirm whether there were any autoscaler events, preemptions, or maintenance in that region? We need ETA and whether you can failover to warm standby.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, GlyphTech

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 17:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected sustained latency & 502s from reserved GPU pool (GlyphTech-prod)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the heads-up and the traces. We're investigating now. Initial telemetry from the allocator shows a backlog forming in the burst allocation path for the reserved pool you mentioned. No scheduled maintenance or preemptions on our side.

Immediate actions we're taking (timeline t=0):
- Engaging on-call infra to snapshot the allocator state and move affected nodes out of rotation for health checks (Marissa).
- Temporarily diverting new burst allocations to the warm standby pool to relieve the queue (Karthik).
- Collecting heap and thread dumps from the allocator process for diagnosis (Soogin).

I'll follow up in 30 min with a status update and next steps. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLAs.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Dedicated Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 18:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected sustained latency & 502s from reserved GPU pool (GlyphTech-prod)

Alicia / Team —

Short update from infra: we identified a deadlock in the burst allocator under high-concurrency path when many small short-lived allocations (sub-200ms) interleave with large requests. Symptoms: queue starvation for steady requests and some requests timing out with 502s. We moved problematic nodes into a health-checking state at 17:40 PT and redirected new burst requests to your warm standby. That reduced tail latency by ~60% but not fully to normal.

We've attached a short timeline (glyphtech_incident_timeline_20271123.pdf) with observed events and node ids. Next steps proposed:
1) Patch the allocator concurrency guard (hotfix) and apply to the pool during a short maintenance window.
2) Increase the burst allocator backoff thresholds to reduce lock contention as a stop-gap.
3) Schedule a follow-up call with GlyphTech SRE to coordinate the maintenance window and failover plan.

I'll propose windows for the patch in my follow-up.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@glyphtech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: GlyphTech SRE <sre@glyphtech.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 19:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected sustained latency & 502s from reserved GPU pool (GlyphTech-prod)

Thanks for the quick triage. Our team confirms reduced error rate after the diversion to warm standby but we're still seeing intermittent 99th spikes on ranking. Can you share the maintenance window options and expected risk? We prefer a short window during US overnight (00:00–04:00 PT) if possible. Also, can you confirm any expected token-level billing implications for the warm-standby diversion?

Diego
SRE Lead, GlyphTech

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@glyphtech.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected sustained latency & 502s from reserved GPU pool (GlyphTech-prod)

Diego / Alicia —

Thank you — and appreciate the preferred window. Proposed mitigation plan:

Planned hotfix window (candidate): Wed 24 Nov 2027 00:30–01:30 PT
- Activity: apply hotfix (hotfix-burst-allocator-20271124.patch) to allocator service on pool rsv-glyph-prod-03, ramp via canary on 2 nodes, then progressively to remainder.
- Risk: low-medium. Canary protects against regressions; brief 1–2 minute connection drains expected per host during service restart.
- Expected outcome: eliminate deadlock, reduce 99th latency to baseline within 15–20 minutes post-rollout.
- Billing: during diversion to warm standby there may be slight token routing differences; we'll reconcile and provide a usage adjustment credit for the impacted window.

Contingency: if patch causes regressions we'll abort and keep diversion to standby while we revert. We'll hold a post-maintenance conference bridge.

Please confirm the window or propose an alternative within 24 hours. We'll provide an incident timeline and a draft postmortem afterward.

— Priyom

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@glyphtech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: GlyphTech SRE <sre@glyphtech.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@glyphtech.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2027 12:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Burst allocator deadlock — reserved capacity queue starvation & action plan

Priyom / Team —

Window confirmed: Wed 24 Nov 2027 00:30–01:30 PT is acceptable. Please keep the canary on and share bridge info. We appreciate the credit offer — our finance team will follow up if anything needs adjustment.

One ask for the postmortem: please include the sequence of client request patterns that triggered the deadlock and any recommended client-side mitigations (e.g., request coalescing, pacing). Knowing what to change on our side will help reduce risk of recurrence while you apply the allocator-level fix.

Thanks,
Alicia
